raw_comment: I noticed that a concerning amount of American states are experiencing some form of drought which is evident in the way the majority of the map is colored and how the least extreme  category is "abnormally dry." I also noticed that New York state is marked as being abnormally dry as is confirmed by the concerning lack of precipitation in my community. I wonder whether the recent hurricanes Helene and Milton decreased the level of drought in the areas they hit and if the drought in these areas was worse before this year's disastrous hurricanes. This relates to me and my community because, like many other states, New York state is abnormally dry. This means that our water supply and crops, which we need to survive, are under threat. Small farmers in my community might not be harvesting as well as before as the land has less moisture than usual. A catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea is "The United States of Drought: Water Scarcity throughout the Country."
